Elaine — following up with the full technical plan inline so you have the primary points for the RFI portal without opening the PDF. The attachment still has reproducible templates and telemetry queries.

Planned migration runbook (detailed):

1) Pre-migration Discovery (3–5 business days)
   - Inventory of endpoints, schema versions, sequence-length distributions, and KV usage.
   - Map heavy-read keys and hot prefixes for cache-warming considerations.
   - Confirm KMS/HSM endpoints per region and any airgap/VPC constraints.

2) Staging & Shadow Phase (10 business days)
   - Deploy Redwood staging with production-sized instance types.
   - Continuous traffic shadowing: replicate 100% reads and a sampled subset (5–10%) of writes to staging for validation.
   - Run data integrity checks: checksums, end-to-end sampling, latency percentiles.

3) Schema Compatibility & Transformation
   - Use transformation layer for forward/backward compatibility. If breaking schema change required, follow three-step compatibility (read-compatible adapters, migration window, deprecation schedule).
   - For database-backed embeddings/metadata stores, perform zero-downtime migration by adding new columns and backfilling in background jobs.

4) Canary Rollout Strategy (7 days)
   - Step 1: 1% of traffic for 12 hours; gate on error rate (<0.5%), p95 latency within SLO (target <200ms), and no data loss on backfill checks.
   - Step 2: 10% for 24 hours; additional gating on downstream system queues and consumer lag.
   - Step 3: 50% for 48 hours; run full telemetry dashboards and contingency drills.
   - At each step we run synthetic scenario tests and an automated rollback if any gate breaches.

5) Dual-write & Fanout / Backfill Patterns
   - Dual-write (recommended for short windows): application writes to both Redwood and legacy store. Idempotent writes and monotonic version stamps ensure consistent state.
   - Backfill (for historical data): parallel bulk backfill with rate-limiting. We prefer batched, victimized backfills that avoid saturating write paths.
   - KV cache warm-up: seed KV with hot prefixes during staging and extend warm-up during canary windows.

6) Cutover & Finalization (5–7 days)
   - Controlled read switch: route reads incrementally from legacy to Redwood once backfill parity metrics are satisfied.
   - Monitoring: short-term increased telemetry retention for 72 hours, with tight alerting for error budget burn.
   - Rollback path: re-enable legacy reads and continue dual-write while investigating. Mean time-to-safe-state estimated at 30–90 minutes for read rollback (dependent on cache TTLs); full operational parity (writes) requires backfill pause and reconciliation (1–4 hours).

7) Observability & Telemetry
   - Prebuilt dashboards: per-route p50/p95/p99 latency, error ratio, token consumption, KV hit rate, downstream consumer lag.
   - Automated regression checks against baseline prompts and a small eval set.

Security & Compliance considerations
   - KMS integration: Redwood supports Bring-Your-Own-KMS; we can integrate with cloud KMS endpoints or HSM for on-prem keys.
   - Data residency: routing policy supports region-bound serving; we can pin models/instances per-region.
   - Audit logs: full request/response audit stream available to your SIEM (configurable retention).

Operational safeguards (gates & kill-switches)
   - Per-canary automatic rollback if gate breached.
   - Manual emergency kill-switch that disables routing to Redwood for a region and flips to fallback model variant.
   - Circuit-breaker thresholds driven by error rate and cost anomalies.

Dependencies & pre-reqs for MercuryTel
   - Network egress rules for Redwood staging and production endpoints.
   - KMS access and key rotation window agreement.
   - Small connector service to handle dual-write idempotency (we can supply a reference implementation).

Estimated timeline (conservative): 5–7 weeks from kickoff for a typical mid-sized integration. We can compress by 1–2 weeks if MercuryTel provides schema inventory and approves early capacity provisioning.

Attachments referenced: RIF-Redwood-Runbook-20270501.pdf (detailed checklist), mapping-template.csv (link in Drive).

If you'd like, I can extract the canary gating logic into a single JSON policy that your deployment orchestration can consume (our ops team has already done this at two banks).

On availability — please propose kickoff windows for Tue/Wed next week; I will block time and include an engineer from our runtime team.

Thanks,

Elaine — answers inline to your two bullets and a couple of practical notes. Forwarding to Ben and Priya to flag procurement and capacity planning.

1) Idempotency guarantees
   - We recommend at-least-once semantics for writes combined with idempotent request IDs and monotonic version stamps on entities. Practical implementation: attach a write-token + entity-version header; if a duplicate arrives the store rejects based on version mismatch. We can provide a reference library for the service shim.

2) KMS/HSM
   - Redwood supports BYO-KMS/HSM where keys never leave the enclave. We integrate via customer-provided HSM endpoints and support signing/unwrap operations over secure channels. We will sign an appendix confirming the integration pattern for procurement.

3) Canary % semantics
   - Canary % is configurable per-route and can be applied per-region; default recommendation is per-region gating so a failure in one region doesn't impact global traffic.

Procurement note: Ben — assigning for reserved capacity sizing and any discount/term questions. Priya — FYI on contract appendix for HSM/KMS wording.

Elaine — I'll add the idempotency reference implementation to the Drive folder and update the RFI PDF with these clarifications.

Thanks,
--
Soojin
